dek: Hadlock Falls is the Acadia National Park waterfall we cover, under Waterfall Bridge on the carriage roads. It runs mainly in spring and autumn, so check the brook first.
overview: Acadia National Park protects the highest rocky headlands on the Atlantic coast of the United States, with 27 miles of historic motor roads, 158 miles of hiking trails and 45 miles of carriage roads.

Hadlock Falls is the waterfall we cover here. USGS says it is "Located in Acadia NP," and the park describes it from Waterfall Bridge, built in 1925, which carries a carriage road over Upper Hadlock Brook at a 40-foot waterfall. The falls aren't always there: the park says they usually appear in spring and autumn, sometimes in early summer after enough rain, and are absent when the brook is low. Our trail file gives 1.2 miles one way on the Hadlock Ponds Trail.
fallsIntro: This is a carriage-road view of a brook that turns on and off, not a waterfall you can count on in August.
plan: The outing is the carriage-road approach in our trail file, 1.2 miles one way. Time it for spring, autumn or a rainy early summer if you want water in the brook. Cadillac Summit Road needs its own vehicle reservation from mid-May into October, but that is a different trip and doesn't apply to this walk.
flow: The nearest gauge is Otter Creek near Bar Harbor (USGS 01022840), about 3.6 miles from Hadlock Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in March at about 8 cubic feet per second and was lowest in July at about 2.
Hadlock Brook is a small carriage-road stream, so Otter Creek is a rainfall cousin rather than a measurement of the brook. The park's note about spring and autumn is the better timing guide.
feesLead: A $35 vehicle pass that must be printed and displayed. The Cadillac Summit Road reservation is separate and not needed for this hike.
access: Entrance passes must be printed and left on the dashboard, and the fee page says cell service is extremely limited, so don't count on showing a pass on your phone. Visitors who aren't US residents pay an additional $100 per person unless they hold an annual or America the Beautiful pass. Bar Harbor is the nearest town in our index, about 5 miles away in a straight line.
safety: The main surprise here is arriving when the brook is dry: the park says there is a waterfall when there is enough water, typically in spring and autumn. We have no cliff or tide warnings for this waterfall on file. The carriage roads are closed to cars.
